segments.text:
This finally we demaund of our aduerſaries, whether they iudge that there is the bodie of the Lord in the bread without bloud, and whether there is bloud in the wine without the bodie? If they ſay, there is, they diuide the humane nature by the two partes of ye myſterie, which cannot be committed without impietie, ſince the bloud & bodie and humane nature of Chriſt are vnited by a perpetuall coniunction. But if they will ſay yt theſe thinges bee together, and will feigne thoſe ſtrāge
Concomitancies of theirs, this at the leaſtwiſe they cannot eſcape but that they ſhal double ye bodie of Chriſt, to wit, wholy vnder the wine, and wholy vnder the bread, appointing the ſame (as they will haue it) vnder their Accidentes.
